title: OpenAI is hiring a power trader, because electricity is now a position on its books
excerpt: OpenAI is recruiting a power-trading lead to hedge electricity and gas costs across its data-centre portfolio, at up to $285,000.
content_html:
OpenAI is recruiting a power-trading lead for its data centres. The role will own commodity hedging strategy across the company’s power portfolio. It will have no direct reports at first.

Bloomberg’s Julian Hast reported the listing on Monday. OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The company’s own job posting places the role on the Power & Land team, inside datacenter design. It pays $181,000 to $285,000 plus equity, and it is open in Seattle, San Francisco or remote.

What the job actually asks for

OpenAI wants at least 10 years in power trading, commodity risk management or utility strategy. It also wants a deep understanding of US wholesale power markets and the natural gas markets attached to them.

The work is recognisably a trading desk. The hire would quantify exposure across markets and sites, then evaluate fixed-price supply, forwards, swaps and options.

They would also build the frameworks for when to hedge and how much. Governance, risk limits and internal controls sit in the same job. Experience with ISDAs and supply contracts is listed as preferred.

OpenAI put the purpose in a single sentence. The role will “translate large, dynamic electricity and fuel exposures into practical hedging, procurement, and risk-management strategies that protect infrastructure economics while preserving flexibility for growth.”

This is ordinary, and that is the point

Hedging a commodity input is not exotic. Food producers hedge coffee and cocoa, airlines hedge jet fuel, manufacturers trade the metals they consume.

What has changed is the category OpenAI now sits in. Electricity has stopped being a line on a monthly bill. It is a market exposure large enough to need its own risk function.

Meta got there first. It said in November 2025 that it was entering power trading to support its AI data centres.

Microsoft and Google face the same constraint. Securing electricity has become one of the hardest limits on the buildout, and the answer increasingly looks like a trading function rather than a procurement one.

Gas is the exposure underneath

More than 40% of US electricity is generated by burning gas. That is why the posting asks for gas expertise alongside power. Hedging one means understanding the other.

Grid connection queues are long, so many data-centre developers are building their own generation while they wait. Meta is hiring for that too. Its careers site lists an energy manager for onsite generation, confirming that “gas supply, land, water, and permitting” are in place.

The environmental arithmetic follows. Meta left RE100, the corporate clean electricity pledge, as gas moved into its data-centre plans.

Why OpenAI needs this now

The committed footprint is what turns power into a risk-management problem. OpenAI is building a Georgia campus worth around $30bn. It has also been in talks over a 10-gigawatt Ohio campus backstopped by Nvidia.

Energy costs have already changed its plans once. The company paused a UK project over electricity prices and regulation.

Regulation is moving underneath all of it. US regulators have been working on a grid fast lane for large loads, which changes when and how these sites can connect.

A job ad is not a strategy

One caveat is worth keeping in view. This is a listing, not an announcement, and OpenAI has not said what it intends to hedge or at what scale.

The role carries no direct reports initially, which reads as a first hire rather than a desk. Whether it grows into one depends on how large the exposure turns out to be.

The salary band is still the tell. A company willing to pay $285,000 for someone fluent in ISDAs and forward curves has stopped thinking of electricity as a utility bill. It is a position on the books now, and positions have to be managed.

content_html_zh:
OpenAI 正在为其数据中心招募一名电力交易主管。 该职位将负责公司电力投资组合的商品对冲策略。 一开始它不会有直接报告。

彭博社的朱利安·哈斯特周一报道了此次上市。 OpenAI 没有立即回应置评请求。

该公司自己的招聘启事将这一职位安排在数据中心设计内部的 Power & Land 团队中。 它支付 181,000 美元到 285,000 美元加上股本，在西雅图、旧金山或偏远地区开放。

这份工作的实际要求是什么

OpenAI 希望在电力交易、商品风险管理或公用事业策略领域拥有至少 10 年的经验。 它还希望深入了解美国批发电力市场及其附属天然气市场。

这件作品显然是一张交易台。 聘用人员将量化跨市场和地点的风险敞口，然后评估固定价格供应、远期、掉期和期权。

他们还将建立何时进行对冲以及对冲金额的框架。 治理、风险限制和内部控制处于同一位置。 有 ISDA 和供应合同经验者优先。

OpenAI 用一句话表达了其目的。 该角色将“将大量、动态的电力和燃料风险转化为实际的对冲、采购和风险管理策略，保护基础设施经济，同时保持增长的灵活性。”

这很平常，这才是重点

对冲商品投入并不陌生。 食品生产商对冲咖啡和可可，航空公司对冲喷气燃料，制造商交易他们消耗的金属。

改变的是 OpenAI 现在所处的类别。 电费不再是每月账单上的一项。 这是一个足够大的市场风险，需要有自己的风险函数。

梅塔首先到达那里。 该公司于 2025 年 11 月表示，将进入电力交易以支持其人工智能数据中心。

微软和谷歌面临着同样的限制。 确保电力安全已成为扩建过程中最困难的限制之一，而答案越来越像是一种交易功能，而不是采购功能。

气体是下面的暴露

美国超过 40% 的电力是通过燃烧天然气产生的。 这就是为什么该职位要求天然气专业知识和电力专业知识。 对冲其中一个意味着理解另一个。

电网连接队列很长，因此许多数据中心开发人员在等待期间正在构建自己的一代。 Meta 也在为此招聘。 其招聘网站列出了现场发电的能源经理，确认“天然气供应、土地、水和许可”均已到位。

环境算术如下。 随着天然气纳入其数据中心计划，Meta 退出了企业清洁电力承诺 RE100。

为什么 OpenAI 现在需要这个

承诺的足迹将权力变成了风险管理问题。 OpenAI 正在乔治亚州建设一个价值约 300 亿美元的园区。 它还在就 Nvidia 支持的 10 吉瓦俄亥俄州园区进行谈判。

能源成本已经改变了一次计划。 该公司因电价和监管问题暂停了一个英国项目。

监管正在这一切的背后进行。 美国监管机构一直致力于为大负荷建立电网快车道，这改变了这些站点的连接时间和方式。

招聘广告不是策略

有一点值得注意。 这是上市，而不是公告，OpenAI 尚未透露打算对冲什么或以什么规模进行对冲。

该职位最初没有直接报告，这看起来像是第一次雇用而不是一个办公桌。 它是否会成长为一种取决于曝光的规模有多大。

薪资范围仍然是最重要的。 一家愿意支付 285,000 美元聘请精通 ISDA 和远期曲线的公司已经不再将电费视为公用事业账单。 现在这是账面上的一个位置，并且必须对位置进行管理。
